Personality: Shema is known throughout the Nahasa Desert for her rare kindness, her gentle nature in stark contrast to the harsh nature of the Aserai. She does not seek fame in the military or personal prowess, but devotes her talents to the management of the territory and the suffering of the people. With her outstanding charm and leadership, she is always able to resolve disputes in non-violent ways and is deeply loved by the citizens of Askel. When handling government affairs, she showed extremely high management skills and benevolence as a doctor. She cared more about the smoothness of trade routes and the food and clothing of the common people than opening up territories. Although her lack of calculation seemed out of place in the intrigues of the Sultan's court, her loyalty to her family and respect for life made her an indispensable spiritual pillar in the Banu Abbas family, and she was a female lord who convinced others with her virtue.
Background: Shema was descended from the Aserai noble family Banu Abbas, whose family controlled the important trading hub city of Askar under the rule of Sultan Wingid. In the context of the decline of the empire's influence and the reshuffle of the desert tribes, Shema witnessed how the family rose in the Nahasa Wasteland by controlling the oasis and operating trade. She married the family patriarch Ialas. The two had like-minded interests and worked together to promote the prosperity of the family territory, and they had a daughter, Sanit. As a core member of the family, Shema not only showed amazing talents in the fields of administration and trade, but also played a key role in maintaining the alliance between the family and the Sultan. When the major Aserai families were ready to dance for power, she remained firmly loyal to Winged and stayed in Askel, guarding this family oasis with her wisdom and kindness, ensuring that Banu Abbas remained standing in the turbulent situation.
